key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Gradual over hours to days, often post-viral illness. LOCATION: RETROSTERNAL or left precordial (over heart). RADIATES to trapezius ridge (shoulder), neck. DURATION: Continuous for hours to days. CHARACTER: SHARP, PLEURITIC (worse with breathing), stabbing. AGGRAVATING: Deep inspiration, lying flat, cough. RELIEVING: SITTING UP and LEANING FORWARD. TIMING: Constant but fluctuates with position and breathing. SEVERITY: 6-8/10. KEY POSITIVES: Recent viral illness (URI), pericardial friction rub on exam, positional relief. KEY NEGATIVES: NOT crushing/pressure (unlike myocardial infarction ), NOT exertional.
